rationale: Interpret the forwarded-route execution (CheckRun 815614d02b874bc8b0661039ae0552da, fixed experiment 6b71731acf2441de9145c5c6f1d03f8b-experiment) that the previous update requested: all seven comparisons resolved - the three premises hold, the witness is violated, and the control, the one-tick bound and the post-window comparison hold - so the second route into the same missing membership check is now measured rather than predicted, and the question's remaining discriminator narrows to routes other than an application-applied removal.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same leading-but-not-the-voter state is reached by a route other than an application-applied removal of the leading node - a leader demoted to learner under the same default, or a joint transition that leaves a single voter - and whether an application reading through the Node wrapper is handed the same stale index as the forwarded requester.

interpretations.rationale: The account rests on three receipts and covers both routes into the same missing membership check. Source side: tracker.IsSingleton is a size test whose comment asserts that the single voting member is the leader (tracker/tracker.go:158-162), stepLeader's MsgReadIndex case answers from that test without any round (raft.go:1354-1361), the answer leaves as a MsgReadIndexResp whenever the request came from another node (raft.go:2072-2087) and a follower forwards its own read to the leader it knows (raft.go:1764-1770), while the write path refuses proposals from exactly this node (raft.go:1294-1303) and applying a committed removal of the leading node leaves it leading under the default StepDownOnRemoval=false (raft.go:1985-2012, 282-287). Local route: in receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 the removed leader answers immediately with an index below what the actual leader had already committed (parsed index 14), the actual leader's own answer covers its commit index (index 4), the exposure ends when it learns of the new term one tick later (index 15) and the next request is not answered (index 16); in the same harness a remainder with two voters leaves the request held in readOnly.unconfirmedReads and never answered. PreVote-only configuration: receipt c72c66880fd9498ca1efb95774b0b06e repeats the singleton shape with CheckQuorum disabled and resolves every comparison, showing that either quorum option alone bounds the window to one heartbeat interval (parsed indices 1-5). Forwarded route: in receipt 815614d02b874bc8b0661039ae0552da the removal again leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose only voter is node 2 (parsed index 1 holds, singleton true, is_voter false, config voters=(2) learners=(3)) while node 2 leads {2} and commits 4 against the removed leader's 2 (index 2 holds); the learner - which still knows node 1 as its leader, still holds the old configuration voters=(1 2) learners=(3) and has no read state of its own - forwards its read to node 1 (index 3 holds, forward_to 1); node 1 answers it with MsgReadIndexResp carrying index 2 to node 3, and the requester consumes that answer as its own read state (index 4 violated: read_index 2 against the actual leader's committed 4); the node that is the configuration's only voter answers its own read with 4 (index 5 holds); one heartbeat tick is enough for the removed leader to learn of the new term and leave the leader state with no leader (index 6 holds, ticks_until_stepdown 1); and the request the requester repeats afterwards is forwarded again and produces no answer at all (index 7 holds, safe_outcome true). The defect statement is now measured on both routes: a node whose own tracker proves it is not the configuration's voter answers a ReadIndex immediately, with no confirmation round, and on the forwarded route the stale index is consumed as another node's read state, so the answer is neither current nor refused.

knowledge.assertion: IsSingleton is a size-only test over the configuration and never compares the single voter with the local node.
StepLeader answers MsgReadIndex locally whenever IsSingleton holds, using its own commit index and without a round.
A removed leader keeps leading by default while its proposals are refused and its read answers are not.
Lease-based reads force CheckQuorum, and the lease makes voters refuse higher-term vote requests while they still hear the leader.

counterevidence: The controls hold in both singleton receipts (parsed index 4 of 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 and index 5 of 815614d02b874bc8b0661039ae0552da: the node that is the configuration's voter answers its own read with an index that covers its commit index), so answering from the singleton test is not itself the defect - the violation depends on the answering node not being that voter.

The measured bounds limit the impact in every quarantine-free configuration tested: with either CheckQuorum or PreVote the removed leader leaves the leader state after one heartbeat tick and stops answering (indices 15-16 of the first receipt, indices 4-5 of the PreVote receipt, indices 6-7 of the forwarded receipt), and ReadOnlyLeaseBased cannot be combined with CheckQuorum disabled, which is the configuration that would extend the window.

The forwarded witness depends on the delivery order that the scenario supplies: the requester's request was issued while node 1 was still the leader it knew and was delivered after the reconfiguration, so the receipt measures a stalled path rather than a requester that keeps choosing a removed node.

The Node.ReadIndex contract tells callers that read index requests can be lost without notice and that retries are their duty (node.go:218-224); the configuration whose remainder has more than one voter is recorded as an accepted-but-unanswered request, and the forward that stops paying is the application's documented remedy.
limitations: Every scenario needs the application to apply the committed change that removes the leading node while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false; an application that sets that option, or that stops the removed node, does not reach the state.

All three witnesses are at the ReadIndex contract level: the receipts show the index handed to the reader (locally, or across the wire as a MsgReadIndexResp) below an entry the actual leader had already committed, and no state machine was run, so a served value that misses that entry is a consequence of the contract rather than a measured value.

The bound is one heartbeat interval at the exercised tick ratio (heartbeat tick 1, election tick 10) and in the two quorum-option settings; other ratios, and a remainder with more than one voter in those settings, are not measured.

The forwarded scenario used a learner as the requester whose request is held across the reconfiguration; other requesters - a removed voter that still knows the old leader, or a follower that simply has not heard from the new one - are not measured.
interpretations.joint_history: All three receipts measure the same removal and read on one fixture family: a small group in which the application proposes and applies the committed removal of the leading node, the removed leader keeps its leadership under the default StepDownOnRemoval=false, the remaining voter becomes leader of the reduced configuration and commits an entry the removed leader never sees, and a ReadIndex request is then delivered to the removed leader with the same decisive endpoints - the configuration the removed leader holds, the index it hands out compared with the new leader's commit index, the number of ticks needed to leave the leader state, and whether a later request is answered. Receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 covers three scenarios of one harness; receipt c72c66880fd9498ca1efb95774b0b06e repeats the CheckQuorum scenario's shape with PreVote only; receipt 815614d02b874bc8b0661039ae0552da uses the same removal and quorum setting as that PreVote harness but adds a learner as the requester and holds its forwarded request across the reconfiguration, so its parsed indices 1-3 establish the same premises as the PreVote receipt's indices 1-2, its index 4 is the same stale-index endpoint as the PreVote receipt's index 3 with the answer now crossing the wire, and its indices 6-7 repeat the PreVote receipt's step-down and post-window outcomes. The three receipts agree on every shared endpoint.
